newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi economy improved in 1995 - SAMA.
newsitem.headline: Saudi economy improved in 1995 - SAMA.

text.p: Firmer oil prices helped Saudi Arabia sharply improve its economic performance in 1995, the kingdom's central bank said on Monday.

The Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency said in an annual report carried on the official Saudi Press Agency that stronger oil prices allowed the kingdom to raise its gross domestic product (GPD) by 4.3 percent, compared to 1.4 percent in 1994.

Saudi Arabia has in recent years suffered cash flow problems due to low oil prices and huge Gulf War costs that prompted it to introduce reforms and tighten public spending. It is also trying to encourage a larger private sector role, privatise some government institutions and boost non-oil exports.
Economists and bankers say the kingdom expects to sharply reduce or even wipe out its budget deficit in 1996 for the first time in more than 10 years.
Saudi Arabia has said its economic reforms were beginning to bear fruit and it expected 6.2 percent GDP growth in 1996.
